title: CREATE TABLE & Storage Parameters
description: Create robust relational tables, configure fillfactor, unlogged tables, and storage options.

data.text: The **`CREATE TABLE`** statement defines the physical schema of an entity. Beyond column definitions and constraints, PostgreSQL supports specialized table storage configurations like `fillfactor` and `UNLOGGED` tables.

An **UNLOGGED table** does not write modifications to the Write-Ahead Log (WAL). This makes inserts and updates 2x-5x faster, at the cost of being truncated automatically if the database crashes. They are ideal for transient sessions, intermediate ETL steps, and cache layers.

data.title: Creating an Unlogged Sessions Table with Custom Fillfactor
data.content: Setting fillfactor to 80% to leave room for HOT updates.

data.text: The following table uses the column features you are expected to know: a generated primary key, `NOT NULL` with a default, a foreign key with an explicit `ON DELETE` action, a check constraint, a generated column, and a composite type — all in one statement.

data.title: Production-Style CREATE TABLE
data.content: Every clause here has a reason; be ready to explain each one.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE orders (
    -- IDENTITY is the SQL-standard replacement for SERIAL
    id           BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id  BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
    status       TEXT   NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
                 CHECK (status IN ('pending','paid','shipped','cancelled')),
    subtotal     NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (subtotal >= 0),
    tax_rate     NUMERIC(5,4)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.20 CHECK (tax_rate BETWEEN 0 AND 1),
    -- generated column: computed on read, cannot be written to
    total        NUMERIC(14,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (subtotal * (1 + tax_rate)) STORED,
    tags         TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    metadata     JSONB  NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    placed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    -- named constraints are far easier to drop or reference later
    CONSTRAINT orders_customer_placed_uniq UNIQUE (customer_id, placed_at)
) WITH (fillfactor = 90);

COMMENT ON TABLE orders IS 'Customer orders; one row per checkout';
COMMENT ON COLUMN orders.tax_rate IS 'Ratio, not a percentage (0.20 = 20%)';

rows: Creates a sequence; column does not own it cleanly
Sequence is owned by the column
You must grant `USAGE` on the sequence separately
Any insert can supply a value
`GENERATED ALWAYS` rejects explicit values unless `OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE`
Percentage of each page filled on insert. Lower values (70–90) leave room for HOT updates and reduce index churn on update-heavy tables.
Per-table override for autovacuum; useful for tiny hot tables or huge append-only tables.
Threshold at which a row is compressed/offloaded to the TOAST table.

data.text: Note that constraints can be added **after** the table exists, which is how large migrations avoid long locks: `ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID;` then `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`.

data.title: Interview Signal
data.text: When asked to design a table, say the parts out loud: pick the primary key type, add `NOT NULL` where the domain demands it, choose an `ON DELETE` action deliberately, and name your constraints so they can be referenced in migrations.

data.title: Design and Create a Schema
data.description: Model a small blog and create it.
steps: Design `users(id, email UNIQUE, created_at)` and `posts(id, author_id, title, body, published_at)`.
Choose `ON DELETE CASCADE` for `author_id` and justify it out loud.
Add a `CHECK` constraint on `published_at` being in the past or null.
Inspect what you created with `\d+ posts` and confirm the index PostgreSQL added for the foreign key.
data.expectedOutcome: A working schema whose constraints encode the business rules rather than relying on application code.

items.question: Should foreign keys always be indexed?
items.answer: The *referenced* side (usually the primary key) is indexed automatically. The *referencing* column is not, and without an index, deletes and updates on the parent do a sequential scan of the child table. Index it unless a composite index covers it.

items.question: What is the difference between `NUMERIC` and `FLOAT` for money?
items.answer: `NUMERIC` is exact decimal arithmetic; `FLOAT`/`DOUBLE PRECISION` are binary floating point and cannot represent 0.10 exactly. Never store money in a float.

items.question: Are table names case-sensitive?
items.answer: Unquoted identifiers are folded to lowercase. `CREATE TABLE Orders` creates `orders`; `CREATE TABLE "Orders"` creates a case-sensitive name that then requires double quotes everywhere.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `CREATE TABLE` establishes columns, types, and constraints.
`UNLOGGED` tables bypass WAL generation for ultra-fast transient operations.
`fillfactor` leaves empty space in data pages to facilitate in-place HOT updates.
